public_rationale: The reviewed records do not establish that only four or five companies rent AI compute at scale. CoreWeave reports substantial aggregate commitments, while Nebius describes strong market demand. Neither supplies the comparable customer-level evidence needed to establish or refute the claimed exclusivity. Provider statements and aggregate backlog cannot settle this market-wide claim.
limitations: Several relevant filings were inaccessible through read_page.
Later customer announcements cannot automatically establish the earlier quarter's customer distribution.

our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns substantial commercial rentals of AI compute, not the existence of small customers or users of AI applications.
The nearby reference to $50 million a year helps explain scale but does not establish a strict threshold for this sentence.
I use January through March 2026, the latest regular reporting quarter available before the July 22 post. Subsequent announcements are context unless they establish facts about that quarter.
Customer diversity requires distinct economic buyers. Resellers and their underlying customers must not be counted twice.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable market-wide evidence shows that substantial AI compute rental demand was effectively confined to four or five economic buyers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes substantial AI compute rentals by materially more than five independent buyers, with a meaningful commercial presence outside the dominant group.
